questions.question: Derived order-of-magnitude electron-count estimate
questions.subtopic: Combine SI prefixes, charge and current for order-of-magnitude estimation
questions.prompt: An electronic sensor carries an approximately constant current of 1.0 mA for about 2.0 ms. Estimate the number of electrons passing a point in that time to the nearest power-of-ten order of magnitude. Take the magnitude of the charge of one electron as 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. Show your working. [4 marks]
markPoints: Convert 1.0 mA = 1.0 × 10⁻³ A and 2.0 ms = 2.0 × 10⁻³ s.
State nearest power-of-ten order of magnitude as 10¹³ electrons.
questions.modelAnswer: Convert the estimates to SI units: I ≈ 1.0 × 10⁻³ A and t ≈ 2.0 × 10⁻³ s. The charge transferred is Q = It ≈ (1.0 × 10⁻³)(2.0 × 10⁻³) = 2.0 × 10⁻⁶ C. The estimated number of electrons is N ≈ Q/e = (2.0 × 10⁻⁶ C)/(1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) = 1.25 × 10¹³. Rounding to the nearest power-of-ten order gives about 10¹³ electrons. These are approximate values and do not justify reporting more precise estimates.
